title: Add client-hiatus reconnect orchestration and soft-cancel window for streaming API
author: Ayesha Patel
release_notes: Adds a configurable client-hiatus window and soft-cancel semantics for streaming sessions; introduces server-side lease refresh and reconnect orchestration. Backwards compatible by default; operators can tighten defaults via config.
description: Motivation: Unreliable client networks and transient disconnects were causing noisy aborts and duplicate tool/function calls in the streaming OpenAI-compat layer. This PR introduces a first-class client-hiatus orchestration mechanism and a "soft-cancel" grace window so that short client disconnects do not immediately finalize sessions or replay tool calls. Design summary: (1) server-side ephemeral lease with configurable 'hiatus_ms' and 'grace_ms' to hold inflight sessions for a short period; (2) an explicit resume handshake: clients present a session token plus a monotonically increasing session-echo to safely rejoin and continue a stream; (3) soft-cancel semantics: when a client disconnects, the server marks a session as 'soft-cancelled' and continues producing a short terminal delta that allows downstream toolcall idempotency guards to commit safely, but it refrains from hard-finalizing model state until grace window expires; (4) lease refresh: long-running streams periodically refresh the ephemeral lease to avoid premature eviction; (5) backoff/jitter tuning: reconnect backoff uses capped exponential with randomized jitter to avoid thundering herd. Implementation notes: added a lightweight orchestrator (server/streaming/hiatus_orchestrator.go) that implements the lease state machine and exposes hooks for the adapter layer. The OpenAI-compat adapter (api/openai_adapter/stream_controller.py) was updated to (a) translate WebSocket disconnects into soft-cancel state, (b) accept resume() calls with session token and session-echo, and (c) enforce idempotent toolcall dedup keys derived from the session-echo + tool-call-id. SDK changes: python SDK exposes Stream.resume(session_token, echo_id) and a new Stream.hiatus_config to mirror server defaults. Console change: admin UI shows 'hiatus_age' and 'soft_cancel' metrics and a toggle for lowering the default grace window per-organization. Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve current behavior for most customers (default grace_ms=20000). Operators can lower to 0ms to restore immediate cancels. Testing: unit tests for state transitions, a deterministic integration harness that simulates network pauses, and end-to-end validations against the python SDK that assert no duplicate toolcall side-effects across reconnects. Rollout plan: feature flagged off by default; staged rollout to Canary (internal), then Dedicated customers with opt-in, then full enable. Metrics to monitor: session_reclaims, resume_success_rate, duplicate_toolcall_rate. Related work: follows ENG-5823 (stream durability) and ENG-5890 (openai-compat reconcilers).

review_conversation: Marco Li (reviewer): The overall approach looks good. Request: tighten the default grace window to 15s instead of 30s — we've seen cases where 30s holds resources too long. Also please add a metric for 'soft_cancel_count' and tag by model.

Ayesha Patel (author): Acknowledged. I've changed the default to 20s to balance operator burden and flaky mobile networks. Added 'soft_cancel_count' and 'hiatus_age_ms' histograms tagged by_model in aa00bb. Willing to make the default configurable via env/values.yaml.

Sofia Nguyen (reviewer): Can you ensure we don't break function/tool call ordering guarantees when a resume happens mid-toolcall? Also add an integration test that simulates duplicate delivery and asserts idempotency guards prevent double-commit.

Ayesha Patel (author): Implemented an idempotent dedupe key using session-echo + tool-call-id and added a deterministic integration in 778899 that replays delivery twice; asserts no duplicate side-effect. Documented the idempotency heuristic in docs/openai_compat_streaming_lifecycle.md.
Daniel Ortiz (reviewer): Code looks good, minor nit on log level for lease refresh telemetry. Approving after nits are addressed.
Ayesha Patel (author): Addressed the logging nit (reduced lease refresh logs to DEBUG) and squashed fixup commits. Ready to merge.

notes_on_upgrade: Default behavior is backward compatible. Operators running private/Dedicated should review charts/values.yaml to lower grace_ms if they have tight GPU capacity constraints. SDK consumers: bump python SDK to v0.8.4 to get resume() helpers. Release flagged; enable via rollout UI or env flag 'STREAM_HIATUS_ENABLED=true'. Monitor resume_success_rate and duplicate_toolcall_rate post rollout.
